body: I think the solution to this is for curl to call OPENSSL_init_ssl with an OPENSSL_INIT_SETTINGS that specifies the same flags to not error on missing config files that it now uses in the call to CONF_modules_load_file. The documentation and historical functionality of CONF_module_load_file seem to indicate it should work, but it clearly doesn't. I'm thinking the intent of the call is to avoid having applications using curl failing unexpectedly, but the current flags will still fail on errors in files it does find, so that goal is perhaps not fully achieved anyway... My proposed change shouldn't change that functionality, hopefully.

I have tested a modified version of curl that has the CONF_module_load replaced with OPENSSL_init_ssl with the same flags (to allow a missing config file) and that makes it work. So I think curl should use the 'modern' apis if openssl version is >= 1.1. I'll provide a PR.
This sounds like a duplicate of #6254 (no crash, so, not exactly..) and I would guess is an OpenSSL issue. Looks like you guessed same openssl/openssl#13548

I think it is both. Curl might be better off not calling this function as there is a newer way of doing it that seems to work, see above. But I think openssl also has a bug that makes it thrash some internal structure if CONF_modules_load(_file) is called twice.

In fact mattcaswell pointed out that not failing on conf errors is now the default in openssl, so I think there is no need to call anything if openssl >= 1.1.0 (or 1.1.1 if the default were not the same in 1.1.0) since the auto-initialization in openssl will just magically call all that is needed.

It's really impossible to keep up with OpenSSL's ideas of how to init their library in different versions.

I read this as saying that with >= 1.1.0  we can set `CURL_DISABLE_OPENSSL_AUTO_LOAD_CONFIG` and it should behave better? Like this:
~~~diff
diff --git a/lib/vtls/openssl.c b/lib/vtls/openssl.c
index fc0c4e15f..dc121feb4 100644
--- a/lib/vtls/openssl.c
+++ b/lib/vtls/openssl.c
@@ -88,10 +88,14 @@
   !defined(OPENSSL_NO_ENGINE) && !defined(OPENSSL_NO_UI_CONSOLE)
 #define USE_OPENSSL_ENGINE
 #include <openssl/engine.h>
 #endif
 
+#if (OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER >= 0x10100000L) /* 1.1.0 or later */
+#define CURL_DISABLE_OPENSSL_AUTO_LOAD_CONFIG
+#endif
+
 #include "warnless.h"
 #include "non-ascii.h" /* for Curl_convert_from_utf8 prototype */
 
 /* The last #include files should be: */
 #include "curl_memory.h"

issue.title: openssl: use OPENSSL_init_ssl() with >= 1.1.0

body: But I have to add I haven't tested with OpenSSL 1.1.0, only 1.1.1

I only have one concern with this: it's a rather big change and historically. changing *anything* in the OpenSSL init sequence will bounce back two months from now when someone has a special OpenSSL build/engine/config that we couldn't test now and that the (lacking) OpenSSL docs certainly don't cover and we have to backpedal again.

If we stick to *only* fix the module load (like #6260 ), it might be a too small fix but it also feels much more conservative and one with a bigger chance of not hitting someone in the face down the road...
I certainly understand those concerns. And this fixes it for me, I'm testing from the PR branch right now. Thx a lot !

Just a note, as you may see in the bug report I made to openssl (https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/13548) the correct way to initialize openssl >= 1.1.0. i.e. code that woks on both 1.1.0 and 1.1.1 would be
OPENSSL_init_ssl(OPENSSL_INIT_LOAD_CONFIG, NULL);
(Thx to mattcaswell for this)

That code would be a no-op if the application using curl had already initialized openssl (which would happen automatically in many cases), but would be needed if you were using 1.1.0 and the application didn't initialize openssl, as it would trigger the loading of the config file which isn't the default with 1.1.0. It would also ignore any errors with both openssl versions.
ok, lets try that then... could be the start of an adventure! :smile:
May I ask what the future holds for this PR ? I'm wondering when it might make it into master and then further into a release.

If you with "this PR" mean #6260, it will be landed as soon as we agree what the proper fix to be. If that happens before December 9, it will ship in the curl 7.74.0 release. If not, it will be be included in the subsequent release etc.

I don't see anything major preventing it from getting merged really soon.
